item.title: Traders Are Dumping Tech Bonds to Make Room for Amazon Debt Deal
item.description: Amazon.com Inc.’s massive bond sale dragged down outstanding hyperscaler debt on Tuesday as investors sold existing securities to fund the new issue, signaling growing fatigue over the barrage of artificial intelligence financings.

item.title: Getty’s Lenders Organize on Renewed Risk of ‘Unsustainable’ Debt
item.description: Lenders to Getty Images Holdings Inc. have started to organize after the debt-laden photo archive business scrapped a planned merger with Shutterstock Inc., according to people familiar with the matter.

item.title: Microsoft Replaces OpenAI, Anthropic With Own AI in Some Apps
item.description: Microsoft Corp., looking to reduce AI costs, is starting to replace OpenAI and Anthropic with its own models in software products like Excel and Outlook.

item.title: Behind Xbox’s Big Layoffs, a Streaming Strategy That Failed
item.description: Microsoft Corp.’s Xbox spent nearly $80 billion in the last decade on deals that would give it popular video game titles like Call of Duty and Skyrim, betting that gamers would flock to its Netflix-like subscription service offering hundreds of options for endless play.

item.title: Gold’s Bull Market Has Ended and Now All Eyes Are on Bears
item.description: A wave of profit taking in the gold market has brought a three-year bull run to an end, but there’s little evidence yet that investors are putting on large-scale short positions in anticipation of further declines.

item.title: BNP Names Jain Global’s Gupta as Head of FICC Trading Americas
item.description: BNP Paribas SA has appointed Kavi Gupta — previously at multistrategy hedge fund Jain Global — as head of fixed income, currencies and commodities trading across the Americas.

item.title: SK Hynix US Listing Said to Be Multiple Times Oversubscribed
item.description: SK Hynix Inc.’s $28 billion US listing is multiple times oversubscribed ahead of pricing on Thursday, according to people familiar with the matter.

item.title: Brazil Treasury Has Patience and Cash to Ease Local Bond Stress
item.description: Brazil’s Treasury is ready to step up actions to alleviate stress in the nation’s 2.3-trillion-real ($447 billion) inflation-linked bond market that has been hit by shifting demand and investors’ concerns about public spending.

item.title: BB Energy Strikes Deal with South Sudan to Unblock Oil Sales
item.description: BB Energy agreed to relax an injunction on the government of South Sudan in exchange for receiving three cargoes of oil, in a significant easing of tensions in the $142 million legal dispute between the trading house and the African nation.

item.title: SpaceX’s Biggest Bull Sees Valuation Soaring Above $10 Trillion
item.description: SpaceX has no shortage of fans on Wall Street, but one analyst stands out among the rest as by far the most bullish: Raymond James’ Brian Gesuale.

item.title: US Consumers’ Inflation Expectations Rose in June, NY Fed Survey Says
item.description: Americans’ expectations for inflation over the near and medium term rose in June amid strong increases anticipated for medical care costs and rent, according to a Federal Reserve Bank of New York survey released Tuesday.

item.title: Rachel Reeves to Attend Brussels Dinner With EU Peers on Energy
item.description: UK chancellor Rachel Reeves will join European Union finance ministers on Thursday in Brussels to discuss energy and economic security matters.

item.title: Treasuries Fall Before Auction as Oil Rebounds, Amazon to Borrow
item.description: Treasuries fell as oil prices climbed on signs of renewed threats to Middle East supply and as Amazon.com slated a corporate bond offering expected to raise at least $25 billion.

item.title: Germany Must Stabilize Debt in Long Run to Keep AAA, Scope Says
item.description: Germany’s debt mountain will need to stop growing in the long term if the country is to retain its top credit grade, according to Scope Ratings.

item.title: Angola Seeks to Raise About $320 Million in Nation’s Biggest IPO
item.description: Angola plans to raise as much as $320 million selling shares in Unitel SA, the country’s biggest telecommunications operator, to help finance its budget and deepen the oil-rich nation’s capital markets.

item.title: Abu Dhabi Royal Family Firm to Invest $1.13 Billion in LNG Company MidOcean
item.description: An investment firm owned by members of Abu Dhabi’s ruling family will invest $1.13 billion in liquefied natural gas company MidOcean Energy LLC.

item.title: Gao, Top China Economist Who Questioned Official GDP Data, Dies
item.description: Influential Chinese economist Gao Shanwen, who challenged the reliability of China’s official growth data and was known for blunt assessments of the economy, has died, according to Chinese media reports.

item.title: Colombia’s Incoming Leader Orders Boycott of Transition Process
item.description: Colombian president-elect Abelardo de la Espriella said he’s suspending transition meetings with the outgoing government, as tensions escalate ahead of the Aug. 7 handover.

item.title: Apollo’s Slok Says S&P 493’s Stalled Margins Are a Big-Tech Risk
item.description: Apollo Global Management Inc.’s Torsten Slok warned that companies outside the giants of the technology sector are failing to show gains in profitability from their spending on artificial intelligence, posing risks to Big Tech valuations.

item.title: BP Drove Up European Jet Fuel Output by 30% During Iran Conflict
item.description: BP Plc boosted jet fuel production at its European refineries by about 30% during the Iran conflict, helping the region avoid major shortages while millions of barrels were locked up in the Persian Gulf.

item.title: Santé Cie Loan Price Jumps as Firm Plans Lender Negotiations
item.description: Traders are rapidly marking up prices for Santé Cie SAS’s loan after the home healthcare provider said it was looking to begin an out-of-court process to negotiate with its lenders.

item.title: German Oil Stocking Agency Says It’s Refilling Strategic Reserve
item.description: Germany’s oil stockpiling agency EBV is looking to refill strategic reserves of diesel, a move that could pile more pressure on an already tight fuel market.

item.title: Apple Supplier Luxshare Prices $3.1 Billion HK Listing at Top
item.description: Apple Inc. supplier Luxshare Precision Industry Co. raised HK$24.3 billion ($3.1 billion) after pricing shares for its Hong Kong listing at the maximum amount it had set.

item.title: Fed’s Williams Stays Optimistic as Energy Prices Fall
item.description: Federal Reserve Bank of New York President John Williams said he expects falling energy prices to drive a drop in overall inflation over the next few months, while reiterating the central bank’s policy is in a good place for now.

item.title: Russian Oil Flows Hit New High But Slumping Prices Crush Income
item.description: Urals prices back where they were before US, Israel launched campaign against Iran

item.title: Dangote Says Kenya Refinery Will Cost as Much as $17 Billion
item.description: A new mega-refinery to be built at the Kenyan coast by Africa’s richest person will cost as much as $17 billion, a spokesman for Dangote Industries Ltd. has confirmed.

item.title: InsuranceDekho Said to Pick Banks for $400 Million India IPO
item.description: Indian insurance aggregator InsuranceDekho’s parent has selected HSBC Holdings Plc, Morgan Stanley, ICICI Securities Ltd. and IIFL Capital Services Ltd. as advisers to a potential initial public offering, according to people familiar with the matter.

item.title: US Trade Deficit Widens to Biggest in More Than a Year
item.description: The US trade deficit widened in May as a broad-based increase in imports and a decline in exports propelled the gap to the most in more than a year.

item.title: UK Lenders Are Exploring Using Riskier Unfunded SRTs, BOE Says
item.description: UK banks are considering unfunded significant risk transfers, according to a report from the Bank of England, which warned that this riskier type of credit hedge is potentially less reliable during times of stress.

item.title: Canada Trade Surplus Highest Since 2022 as War Fuels Exports
item.description: Canada’s trade surplus widened to its largest in four years as the country’s energy, metals and mineral sectors helped fill global supply gaps left by disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz.
